summary_hint: VA COE for {veteran name}, entitlement code {code}, {available_entitlement_amount} available, funding fee {exempt/not exempt}, issued {coe_issue_date}.

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: identity — source is VA / a Regional Loan Center; authenticity check

typed_core.name: regional_loan_center_or_issuer
typed_core.why: disambiguator for issuer_name (which VA RLC issued it)

typed_core.name: veteran_or_service_member_name
typed_core.why: identity — whose eligibility this is (flattened from person)

typed_core.name: social_security_number_masked
typed_core.why: PII — attaches COE to the borrower; last-4 identity match
typed_core.prompt_hint: SSN on a COE is normally masked to last-4 — extract as printed; never infer full digits

typed_core.name: coe_issue_date
typed_core.why: identity — which issuance of the COE

typed_core.name: entitlement_code
typed_core.why: processor — entitlement category drives eligibility interpretation
typed_core.prompt_hint: 'Entitlement code' is a two-digit VA code — extract verbatim, do not interpret

typed_core.name: available_entitlement_amount
typed_core.why: processor — the headline number for loan sizing / second-tier entitlement

typed_core.name: funding_fee_exempt_indicator
typed_core.why: processor — whether the VA funding fee applies

typed_core.name: funding_fee_exemption_reason
typed_core.why: disambiguator for the exempt indicator (why exempt: disability, Purple Heart)

typed_core.name: restoration_status
typed_core.why: processor — whether prior entitlement was restored

nested_lists.name: prior_va_loan_or_entitlement_charges
nested_lists.shape_reason: a COE lists prior VA loans that charged entitlement; count is small (typically 0-4), so a flat row per prior loan is cheap and well under the 16,384 ceiling. Serves no rule today; retained for processor entitlement math

fields.name: prior_loan_reference
fields.why: identifies the prior VA loan that charged entitlement

fields.name: entitlement_amount_charged
fields.why: the entitlement amount charged by the prior loan; feeds remaining-entitlement math

fields.name: prior_loan_status
fields.why: paid-in-full / active — bears on whether entitlement was restored

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date
rejected.reason: duplicate coe_issue_date; a COE has no closing-relevant expiration

rejected.name: property_address, loan_number, account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: a COE is not property- or loan-specific

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: a COE is system-issued, not executed

rejected.name: service_dates (date_range[])
rejected.reason: no coercer for date_range; low value; catch-all

encoding_variations: Entitlement is stated as a code (e.g. '05', '10') that maps to an entitlement category — the code alone is meaningless without the VA code table; keep entitlement_code verbatim.

Funding-fee exemption appears three ways: an explicit exempt flag, a prose reason ('exempt — service-connected disability'), or a disability rating implying exemption. Keep both funding_fee_exempt_indicator and funding_fee_exemption_reason so a bare flag is trusted.
Entitlement amounts may be printed as '$36,000 basic' plus a bonus/second-tier figure — capture basic and available separately.

open_questions.q: prior_va_loan_or_entitlement_charges shape. Item count is small but unbounded.
open_questions.recommendation: flat-row — a processor computing remaining entitlement needs it structured, and cost is low GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): BUILD IT — LP-437 made nested lists cheap (one declaration + the generic mechanism); the one-list-budget / defer / no-consumer concern is overturned. Build as flat_row; the per-rule consumer is separate follow-up.

open_questions.q: Is a COE ever consumed by a rule? Today zero rules. If a future VA-eligibility rule lands, available_entitlement_amount and funding_fee_exempt_indicator become the floor.
open_questions.recommendation: they are already promoted, so no re-extraction needed. Confirm with domain expert

open_questions.q: va_file_or_loan_number PII class. Confidential but not SSN-class. Register in _PII_FIELDS or leave as a plain typed field?
open_questions.recommendation: plain typed field, flagged GEET'S DECISION (LP-438): mask account-like identifiers (policy/account/plan numbers, wire/ACH trace, check references) via _PII_FIELDS; leave addresses and public-record case numbers PLAIN; DOB is unmasked (pii null).

notes: No rules read this document today, so there is no rule floor. The VA Certificate of Eligibility is the gating document for a VA loan: it establishes the veteran, their entitlement, and whether the funding fee applies.
social_security_number_masked needs _PII_FIELDS registration, pre_masked true (COE prints last-4 only). Not in the current 7-field registry.
va_file_or_loan_number is a confidential identifier — treat as a typed field (not catch-all) but not SSN-class PII; flag for review rather than auto-registering.
Prompt hint (doc-level): tell the model this is a VA Form 26-8320 / 26-8320a class document; issuer is the Department of Veterans Affairs, not a private lender.

The nested list prior_va_loan_or_entitlement_charges fields (prior_loan_reference, entitlement_amount_charged, prior_loan_status) are inferred — the design doc describes the list in prose but does not enumerate its fields.
Ambiguity: va_file_or_loan_number PII class is unresolved (Open question 3) — carried as reason_class identity with pii null, pending the register-or-plain decision.
